sentences.en: Dr. Berry, take us back to June 19th, 1865, and what happened that day.
sentences.zh: 贝里博士，请带我们回到1865年6月19日，那天发生了什么？

sentences.en: For most enslaved people in Texas, it was a typical day.
sentences.zh: 对于德克萨斯州的大多数被奴役者来说，那本是平常的一天。

sentences.en: They got up, they went to the fields, or picking cotton, or producing sugar, and working just as they always had done.
sentences.zh: 他们起床，去田里干活，采摘棉花或生产糖，像往常一样劳作。

sentences.en: This was two months after the Civil War ended and two and a half years after the Emancipation
sentences.zh: 那时距离内战结束已经过去了两个月，距离林肯总统在1863年1月1日发布的《解放

sentences.en: Proclamation that President Lincoln issued on January 1st of 1863.
sentences.zh: 黑人奴隶宣言》也已经过去了两年半。

sentences.en: Although they were fighting for their freedom, although they were still running away and committing acts of day-to-day resistance
sentences.zh: 尽管他们一直在为自由而战，尽管他们仍在逃亡并进行日常的抵抗，

sentences.en: on plantations, enslaved people were not actually living in freedom.
sentences.zh: 但在种植园里，被奴役的人们实际上并没有生活在自由之中。

sentences.en: But on that day, June 19th of
sentences.zh: 但在那一天，1865年6月19日，

sentences.en: 1865, General Gordon Granger of the Union Army galloped into Galveston with 2,000 other individuals and came and gave a proclamation.
sentences.zh: 联邦军队的戈登·格兰杰将军带着2000名士兵骑马进入加尔维斯顿，并发布了一项公告。

sentences.en: The people of Texas, Granger said, are informed that in accordance with a proclamation from the Executive of the United States, slaves are free.
sentences.zh: 格兰杰说，德克萨斯州的人民被告知，根据美国行政部门的公告，奴隶们自由了。

sentences.en: This involves an absolute equality of personal rights and rights of property between former masters and slaves.
sentences.zh: 这意味着前奴隶主与奴隶之间在人权和财产权上享有绝对的平等。

sentences.en: And the connection heretofore existing between them becomes that between employer and hired laborer.
sentences.zh: 此前存在于他们之间的关系，现在变成了雇主与雇佣劳工的关系。

sentences.en: Formerly enslaved people, when they heard the news that slavery was over in Texas, celebrated.
sentences.zh: 当曾经被奴役的人们听到德克萨斯州奴隶制终结的消息时，他们欢呼雀跃。

sentences.en: It was a day of great jubilee.
sentences.zh: 那是一个盛大的庆典日。

sentences.en: They danced, they sung, they fled their plantations.
sentences.zh: 他们跳舞、歌唱，逃离了种植园。

sentences.en: It was them claiming their freedom.
sentences.zh: 那是他们对自由的宣示。

sentences.en: It was them going out and embracing it.
sentences.zh: 那是他们走出去拥抱自由。

sentences.en: It was them packing their bags and leaving.
sentences.zh: 那是他们收拾行囊离开。

sentences.en: It was them hugging their loved ones and saying, we're free, we're finally free.
sentences.zh: 那是他们拥抱亲人，说着：我们自由了，我们终于自由了。

sentences.en: In the 1930s, the Workers' Progress Administration interviewed formerly enslaved people and asked them to tell their stories of slavery.
sentences.zh: 20世纪30年代，公共事业振兴署采访了曾经被奴役的人们，让他们讲述自己的奴隶生涯。

sentences.en: Many recalled June
sentences.zh: 许多人回忆起6月

sentences.en: 19th, particularly those that had been enslaved in Texas.
sentences.zh: 19日，特别是那些在德克萨斯州被奴役的人。

sentences.en: We learn decades later of their experience and their response to when they learned about freedom.
sentences.zh: 几十年后，我们才了解到他们的经历，以及他们得知获得自由时的反应。

sentences.en: Sarah Ford said, when freedom come, I didn't know what that was.
sentences.zh: 莎拉·福特说，当自由来临时，我不知道那是什么意思。

sentences.en: Her uncle came to the yard and yelled, everybody free, everybody free.
sentences.zh: 她叔叔跑到院子里大喊：大家都自由了，大家都自由了。

sentences.en: And pretty soon, soldiers comes and the captain reads the proclamation.
sentences.zh: 很快，士兵们来了，长官宣读了公告。

sentences.en: Others like Molly Farrell, a Texas bondwoman said, everybody talk about freedom and hope to get free before they die.
sentences.zh: 其他人，比如德克萨斯州的被奴役者莫莉·法雷尔说，每个人都在谈论自由，希望在死前获得自由。

sentences.en: Me and my mother left right off.
sentences.zh: 我和我母亲立刻就离开了。

sentences.en: Most everybody else goes with us.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有其他人都跟着我们一起走。

sentences.en: We walk down the road, singing and shouting to a beat of the band.
sentences.zh: 我们走在路上，伴着乐队的节奏唱歌欢呼。

sentences.en: My father comes the next day and joins us.
sentences.zh: 我父亲第二天也赶来加入了我们。

sentences.en: Sarah Ashley recalled, I was 19 years old when the burst of freedom come in June and I get turned loose.
sentences.zh: 莎拉·阿什利回忆道：6月自由降临时我19岁，我获得了释放。

sentences.en: Her former enslaver said that they were welcome to stay, except her father felt like they wanted to leave.
sentences.zh: 她以前的奴隶主说欢迎他们留下，但她父亲觉得他们想离开。

sentences.en: Sarah recalls,
sentences.zh: 莎拉回忆说：

sentences.en: Papa left, but he came back with a wagon and mules.
sentences.zh: 爸爸离开了，但他带着马车和骡子回来了。

sentences.en: When he borrows and he loads up mama and my sister and me and us goes to East Columbia on the Brazos River and we settled down.
sentences.zh: 他借来马车，装上妈妈、我和我妹妹，我们去了布拉索斯河畔的东哥伦比亚，在那里定居下来。

sentences.en: They hired out my time, gave us a patch of land.
sentences.zh: 他们雇佣我干活，给了我们一小块地。

sentences.en: And for the first time I ever seed money.
sentences.zh: 那是我第一次见到钱。

sentences.en: Papa builds us a cabin and a corn crib and us show happy because the bright light done come and there was no more weapons.
sentences.zh: 爸爸为我们盖了一间小屋和一个玉米仓，我们非常高兴，因为光明已经到来，再也没有武器了。

sentences.en: Within a year, when formerly enslaved people are celebrating Juneteenth, they're also facing grave restrictions
sentences.zh: 一年之内，当曾经被奴役的人们庆祝六月节时，他们也因为1866年的《黑人法典》而面临严酷的限制，

sentences.en: upon their lives because of the 1866 Black Codes, which restricted African Americans from doing everyday activities, restricted them from where they could go.
sentences.zh: 这些法典限制了非裔美国人的日常活动，限制了他们的行动范围。

sentences.en: They actually predated Jim Crow legislation.
sentences.zh: 这些法典实际上早于吉姆·克劳法。

sentences.en: This was also the same year that the Ku Klux Klan was founded in Poluski, Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 同一年，三K党也在田纳西州的普拉斯基成立了。

sentences.en: But African Americans that were formerly enslaved in Texas celebrated on.
sentences.zh: 但德克萨斯州曾经被奴役的非裔美国人依然继续庆祝。

sentences.en: They celebrated Juneteenth in their backyards, in their churches, in their communities.
sentences.zh: 他们在后院、教堂和社区里庆祝六月节。

sentences.en: They had barbecues and picnics and celebrated and remembered.
sentences.zh: 他们举行烧烤和野餐，庆祝并铭记。

sentences.en: They remembered the institution of slavery.
sentences.zh: 他们铭记奴隶制度。

sentences.en: Elders came and talked to the young children and told them about their experiences with slavery and wanted them to recognize the importance and the significance of emancipation.
sentences.zh: 长辈们会来和孩子们交谈，讲述他们经历的奴隶生活，并希望他们认识到解放的重要性和意义。

sentences.en: Because of the Great Migration, African Americans that lived in Texas moved to other parts of the United States and they brought the celebration
sentences.zh: 由于大迁徙，居住在德克萨斯州的非裔美国人搬到了美国其他地区，他们也把

sentences.en: of Juneteenth Emancipation Day with them.
sentences.zh: 六月节解放日的庆祝活动带到了那里。

sentences.en: But then in the 1920s, 30s, and 40s, because of Jim Crow laws,
sentences.zh: 但在20世纪20、30和40年代，由于吉姆·克劳法，

sentences.en: African Americans celebrated Juneteenth in private settings, in their homes and in their churches.
sentences.zh: 非裔美国人在私人场合、家中和教堂里庆祝六月节。

sentences.en: They were restricted in terms of parks and public spaces.
sentences.zh: 他们在公园和公共场所受到限制。

sentences.en: They could not go to movie theaters except for on certain days and they had to enter through certain doors.
sentences.zh: 除了特定的日子，他们不能去电影院，而且必须从特定的门进入。

sentences.en: They were restricted from amusement parks, water fountains, lunch counters.
sentences.zh: 他们被禁止进入游乐园、使用饮水机和午餐柜台。

sentences.en: All forms of segregation forced African Americans into their own communities.
sentences.zh: 各种形式的种族隔离迫使非裔美国人只能在自己的社区内活动。

sentences.en: And in these spaces, during the heart of Jim Crow segregation, African Americans celebrated
sentences.zh: 在这些空间里，在吉姆·克劳种族隔离制度的核心时期，非裔美国人

sentences.en: Juneteenth privately.
sentences.zh: 私下里庆祝六月节。

sentences.en: The resurgence of the public version of Juneteenth returns in the 1960s with the
sentences.zh: 六月节的公开庆祝活动在20世纪60年代随着

sentences.en: Civil Rights Movement and the Black Power Movement.
sentences.zh: 民权运动和黑人权力运动而复兴。

sentences.en: The Black Power Movement disseminated ideas about
sentences.zh: 黑人权力运动传播了

sentences.en: Black is beautiful.
sentences.zh: “黑人即美丽”的理念。

sentences.en: Black people embrace the way they looked.
sentences.zh: 黑人开始拥抱自己的外貌。

sentences.en: The reason for it, you might say, is like a new awareness among black people that their own natural appearance, physical appearance, is beautiful.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，其原因在于黑人中产生了一种新的意识，即他们自然的、身体的外貌是美丽的。

sentences.en: Their hair, their clothing.
sentences.zh: 他们的头发，他们的服装。

sentences.en: Dig it?
sentences.zh: 懂了吗？

sentences.en: Isn't it beautiful?
sentences.zh: 难道不美吗？

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Freedom and justice.
sentences.zh: 自由与正义。

sentences.en: I have a dream that my four little children will one day live in a nation where they will not be judged by the color of their skin, but by the content of their character.
sentences.zh: 我有一个梦想，我的四个孩子有一天将生活在一个国家，他们不会因为肤色而被评判，而是因为他们的品格。

sentences.en: I have a dream today.
sentences.zh: 我今天有一个梦想。

sentences.en: At this time, African Americans were celebrating victories from the Civil Rights Movement.
sentences.zh: 当时，非裔美国人正在庆祝民权运动的胜利。

sentences.en: Now, in this summer of 1964, the Civil Rights Bill is the law of the land.
sentences.zh: 现在，在1964年的这个夏天，《民权法案》已成为国家法律。

sentences.en: In the words of the president, it restricts no one's freedom so long as he respects the rights of others.
sentences.zh: 用总统的话说，只要一个人尊重他人的权利，它就不会限制任何人的自由。

sentences.en: And they then started becoming more and more public about their celebrations with Juneteenth festivals.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们开始通过六月节庆典，更加公开地进行庆祝活动。

sentences.en: Residents of Resurrection City and my fellow citizens.
sentences.zh: 复活城的居民们，我的同胞们。

sentences.en: One particular celebration occurred on June 19th of 1968.
sentences.zh: 其中一个特别的庆祝活动发生在1968年6月19日。

sentences.en: I stand here today with many mixed emotions.
sentences.zh: 今天我怀着复杂的心情站在这里。

sentences.en: The D.C.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿特区

sentences.en: Urban League invited Coretta Scott King to speak on that day.
sentences.zh: 城市联盟邀请科雷塔·斯科特·金在当天发表演讲。

sentences.en: For it was five years ago that my late husband, Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., stood in this very spot and told the nation about his dream.
sentences.zh: 因为五年前，我的亡夫马丁·路德·金博士正是站在这里，向全国讲述了他的梦想。

sentences.en: A mourning wife, a grieving mother, is talking to a crowd of 75,000 people about African American freedom and the freedom of all people.
sentences.zh: 一位哀悼的妻子，一位悲伤的母亲，正在向7.5万名群众讲述非裔美国人的自由以及所有人的自由。

sentences.en: Perhaps racism can be traced to that dark period in our history when slavery became institutionalized for 244 years.
sentences.zh: 种族主义或许可以追溯到我们历史上那段黑暗时期，当时奴隶制被制度化了244年。

sentences.en: The roots of racism, she reminded us, deprived African Americans and other poor people of color
sentences.zh: 她提醒我们，种族主义的根源剥夺了非裔美国人和其他贫困有色人种的

sentences.en: dignity, self-respect, jobs, and they often experience violence by the hands of white Americans.
sentences.zh: 尊严、自尊和工作机会，他们还经常遭受美国白人的暴力侵害。

sentences.en: The road to justice, peace, and brotherhood is difficult.
sentences.zh: 通往正义、和平与兄弟情谊的道路是艰难的。

sentences.en: We must renew our strength, increase our faith, and gird our courage.
sentences.zh: 我们必须重振力量，增加信仰，鼓起勇气。

sentences.en: People left this particular celebration and brought it back to their homes in their states throughout the country.
sentences.zh: 人们离开了这次特别的庆祝活动，并将其带回了全国各地的家中。

sentences.en: And in this moment, African Americans are embracing and celebrating Juneteenth.
sentences.zh: 在这一刻，非裔美国人正在拥抱和庆祝六月节。

sentences.en: They're celebrating it because they're taking pride in their culture, they're remembering a difficult part of their history, the history of slavery,
sentences.zh: 他们庆祝是因为他们为自己的文化感到自豪，他们在铭记历史中艰难的一部分，即奴隶制的历史，

sentences.en: and they're recognizing freedom and equality.
sentences.zh: 并且他们在认可自由与平等。

sentences.en: Juneteenth becomes a state holiday in Texas officially in 1980.
sentences.zh: 1980年，六月节正式成为德克萨斯州的州立节日。

sentences.en: And from this moment on, celebrations from Juneteenth become much more public.
sentences.zh: 从那一刻起，六月节的庆祝活动变得更加公开。

sentences.en: Large-scale parades, barbecues, picnics, African Americans are celebrating and sharing the stories
sentences.zh: 大型游行、烧烤、野餐，非裔美国人庆祝并分享

sentences.en: of slavery, sharing the history of slavery, and sharing oral histories from those that remember celebrations from years ago.
sentences.zh: 奴隶制的故事，分享奴隶制的历史，并分享那些记得多年前庆祝活动的人们的口述历史。

sentences.en: Another widely publicized incident captured on videotape has become a focus for ethnic tensions between the Black and Korean communities in Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 另一起被录像带捕捉到的广受关注的事件，成为了洛杉矶黑人和韩裔社区之间种族紧张关系的焦点。

sentences.en: Then there came a moment in the early 1990s where Juneteenth celebrations took on new meanings.
sentences.zh: 后来，在20世纪90年代初，六月节的庆祝活动有了新的含义。

sentences.en: March 16th, 1991.
Latasha Harlins, a Black teenager, is shot and killed by a Korean store owner, Soon-Ja-Doo.
sentences.zh: 黑人少女拉塔莎·哈林斯被韩裔店主斗顺子枪杀。

sentences.en: Do claim Harlins was stealing a bottle of orange juice when she confronted the teenager.
sentences.zh: 斗顺子声称哈林斯在与她对峙时正试图偷一瓶橙汁。

sentences.en: The merchant, Soon-Ja-Doo, was convicted of voluntary manslaughter.
sentences.zh: 店主斗顺子被判过失杀人罪。

sentences.en: Her sentence, five years probation, no jail time.
sentences.zh: 她的刑罚是五年缓刑，无需入狱。

sentences.en: The Black community is outraged.
sentences.zh: 黑人社区感到愤怒。

sentences.en: And it sends a bad message that a human life is not valued.
sentences.zh: 这传递了一个糟糕的信息，即人的生命没有价值。

sentences.en: What, six months probation?
sentences.zh: 什么，六个月缓刑？

sentences.en: I mean, the people were pissed then.
sentences.zh: 我是说，当时人们气疯了。

sentences.en: The title of this videotape is very appropriate.
sentences.zh: 这段录像带的标题非常贴切。

sentences.en: It's called the Foothill Incident.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“富山事件”。

sentences.en: By now, like every man, woman, and child in probably the United States, you have witnessed this videotape in your own living rooms over and over again.
sentences.zh: 到现在，可能美国每一个男人、女人和孩子，都在自己的客厅里一遍又一遍地目睹了这段录像。

sentences.en: A bystander videotaped the policeman shocking 25-year-old Rodney King with a stun gun, then clubbing and kicking him as he lay on the ground.
sentences.zh: 一名旁观者拍摄了警察用电击枪电击25岁的罗德尼·金，然后在他倒地时对他进行殴打和踢踹的视频。

sentences.en: Against a growing national furor over last weekend's police beating of an unarmed black motorist,
sentences.zh: 针对上周末警察殴打一名手无寸铁的黑人司机的事件，全国范围内激起了日益高涨的愤怒，

sentences.en: Los Angeles Police Chief Daryl Gates said today that all 14 officers involved will be disciplined and that three will face criminal charges.
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶警察局长达里尔·盖茨今天表示，所有涉案的14名警官都将受到纪律处分，其中三人将面临刑事指控。

sentences.en: These two incidents sparked unrest in the community.
sentences.zh: 这两起事件引发了社区的动荡。

sentences.en: But after the King beating, African Americans were once again on alert.
sentences.zh: 但在金被殴打后，非裔美国人再次处于戒备状态。

sentences.en: Thirty-five days of testimony, 54 witnesses.
sentences.zh: 35天的证词，54名证人。

sentences.en: The video played scores of times in real-time, slow motion, frame by frame.
sentences.zh: 这段视频被实时、慢动作、逐帧播放了无数次。

sentences.en: Finally, the jurors leave to deliberate.
sentences.zh: 最后，陪审员们离开去进行审议。

sentences.en: Well, my reaction is shock first and then disappointment.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的第一反应是震惊，然后是失望。

sentences.en: Obviously, we feel the evidence warranted a conviction on the defendants and the jury disagreed with us.
sentences.zh: 显然，我们认为证据足以让被告定罪，但陪审团不同意我们的看法。

sentences.en: And we must abide by their decision.
sentences.zh: 我们必须遵守他们的决定。

sentences.en: All the police officers involved in the beating of Rodney King were acquitted, and that led to the Los Angeles riots.
sentences.zh: 所有参与殴打罗德尼·金的警官都被判无罪，这导致了洛杉矶骚乱。

sentences.en: The violence erupted after the acquittal of four white policemen in the beating trial of black motorist Rodney King.
sentences.zh: 在黑人司机罗德尼·金的殴打案审判中，四名白人警察被判无罪，随后暴力事件爆发。

sentences.en: We're being told that several patrol cars have been surrounded near Parker Center downtown.
sentences.zh: 我们被告知，市中心帕克中心附近有几辆巡逻车被包围了。

sentences.en: All of the officers in the Central Division are being instructed to put on their helmets with shields in the area near the police headquarters.
sentences.zh: 中央分局的所有警官都被指示在警察总部附近区域戴上带有面罩的头盔。

sentences.en: I feel that there is an undercurrent of racism and that the system has wrought into the court.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有一种潜在的种族主义，而且这种制度已经渗透到了法庭中。

sentences.en: No justice!
sentences.zh: 没有正义！

sentences.en: No peace!
sentences.zh: 就没有和平！

sentences.en: No justice!
sentences.zh: 没有正义！

sentences.en: If we're looking at you, we can tell you now at least five major fires have broken out in South Central.
sentences.zh: 如果我们看着你，我们现在可以告诉你，南中央区至少爆发了五起大火。

sentences.en: There were so many blazes, the fire department couldn't respond to all the calls and just let some buildings burn to the ground.
sentences.zh: 火灾太多了，消防部门无法应对所有的报警，只能任由一些建筑物烧成灰烬。

sentences.en: Yes, they saw law-abiding citizens expressing their anger at the verdict.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们看到守法公民表达对判决的愤怒。

sentences.en: And they chose as an opportunity to steal, to loot, to vandalize, and indeed to kill.
sentences.zh: 而他们却选择以此为机会进行偷窃、抢劫、破坏，甚至杀人。

sentences.en: That we cannot and will not tolerate.
sentences.zh: 这是我们无法也不会容忍的。

sentences.en: As in 1968, after the Rodney King beating, there was a resurgence in the celebration of Juneteenth,
sentences.zh: 就像1968年罗德尼·金遭殴打事件后，六月节的庆祝活动再次兴起一样，

sentences.en: because African Americans were thinking about freedoms and thinking about civil rights and thinking about Rodney King.
sentences.zh: 因为非裔美国人在思考自由、民权以及罗德尼·金的遭遇。

sentences.en: They wanted to celebrate and focus on African American liberty, African American justice, and they felt like Rodney King did not receive justice.
sentences.zh: 他们想要庆祝并关注非裔美国人的自由与正义，而他们觉得罗德尼·金并没有得到公正对待。

sentences.en: So Juneteenth celebrations were celebrations to recognize freedom and recognize enslavement at the same time.
sentences.zh: 所以，六月节的庆祝活动既是为了纪念自由，也是为了铭记奴役。

sentences.en: So the story of Juneteenth, from what you're saying, is cyclical.
sentences.zh: 照你这么说，六月节的故事是循环往复的。

sentences.en: It's the story of cycles of joy and pain living side by side.
sentences.zh: 这是一个喜悦与痛苦并存的循环故事。

sentences.en: And the last time that Juneteenth experienced a major resurgence began with this scene of police brutality and systemic racism broadcast to the entire country.
sentences.zh: 而上一次六月节的大规模复兴，正是始于这起警察暴力和系统性种族歧视事件在全国范围内的传播。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: We saw this the very first year Juneteenth was celebrated, in the 1860s, against the backdrop of both joy and pain, of slavery and freedom.
sentences.zh: 我们在19世纪60年代六月节首次被庆祝时就看到了这一点，那是在喜悦与痛苦、奴役与自由的背景下进行的。

sentences.en: We saw this in the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 我们在20世纪60年代也看到了这一点。

sentences.en: We saw this again in the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 我们在20世纪90年代再次看到了这一点。

sentences.en: And we're seeing this again today.
sentences.zh: 而今天我们又一次看到了。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了吗？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《纽约时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能让你免费试用一个月，且无需绑定信用卡，去探索《纽约时报》呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《纽约时报》的订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载应用程序，获取30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Dr. Berry, here we are.
sentences.zh: 那么，贝里博士，我们现在身处此地。

sentences.en: It's about 30 years after Rodney King.
sentences.zh: 距离罗德尼·金事件已经过去大约30年了。

sentences.en: And we are in the middle of another national outcry over police violence and systemic racism.
sentences.zh: 我们正处于另一场关于警察暴力和系统性种族歧视的全国性抗议之中。

sentences.en: And it is now June 19th, 2020, Juneteenth.
sentences.zh: 现在是2020年6月19日，六月节。

sentences.en: And I know that this may be a bit of an unfair question to ask a historian without the benefit of time and of distance.
sentences.zh: 我知道，在没有时间和距离优势的情况下问历史学家这个问题可能有点不公平。

sentences.en: But what does this day mean right now, in this moment?
sentences.zh: 但在这个时刻，这一天意味着什么？

sentences.en: For me as a historian, it means celebrating African-American freedom and African-American restraints that are put upon us as a people.
sentences.zh: 作为一名历史学家，对我来说，这意味着庆祝非裔美国人的自由，同时也反思作为这个民族我们所受到的束缚。

sentences.en: It is a moment where we celebrate gains and losses.
sentences.zh: 这是一个我们庆祝收获与承受损失的时刻。

sentences.en: We're seeing African-Americans today being beaten the same way we did in the 1990s, the same way we did in the 60s, and in the 1860s.
sentences.zh: 我们今天看到的非裔美国人遭受殴打的情况，与我们在90年代、60年代以及19世纪60年代所见如出一辙。

sentences.en: We're seeing African-American life being devaluated by not only police officers, but also citizens who feel like they have the right to challenge and confront African-Americans
sentences.zh: 我们看到非裔美国人的生命不仅被警察贬低，也被那些自认为有权质问和对抗非裔美国人的普通公民所贬低，

sentences.en: for doing everyday mundane tasks.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为他们做着日常琐事。

sentences.en: Black people are being killed in their living rooMs.
sentences.zh: 黑人在自己的客厅里被杀害。

sentences.en: They're being killed in their backyards.
sentences.zh: 他们在自己的后院被杀害。

sentences.en: They're being killed on the streets.
sentences.zh: 他们在街头被杀害。

sentences.en: And they're being killed sleeping in their cars.
sentences.zh: 他们在车里睡觉时被杀害。

sentences.en: They're being killed for going and purchasing some Skittles or playing with a toy gun in a park.
sentences.zh: 他们因为去买彩虹糖或在公园里玩玩具枪而被杀害。

sentences.en: I have these conversations, and these conversations mean so much to me as a mother who has an African-American teenage young man in my household.
sentences.zh: 我进行过这些对话，作为家里有一位非裔美国青少年儿子的母亲，这些对话对我意义重大。

sentences.en: And so what has that conversation been like with your son?
sentences.zh: 那么，你和你儿子的对话是怎样的？

sentences.en: Very difficult conversations with him.
sentences.zh: 是非常艰难的对话。

sentences.en: The fear of the police and what to do if he's confronted.
sentences.zh: 关于对警察的恐惧，以及如果被警察拦下该怎么办。

sentences.en: We had that conversation with him when he was 12.
sentences.zh: 他在12岁时我们就和他进行过那次谈话。

sentences.en: And it's been hard because we have very close friends that are police officers.
sentences.zh: 这很艰难，因为我们有非常亲密的朋友是警察。

sentences.en: So it's a very mixed conversation, you know, to have with him and to talk to him about how to interact,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，和他谈论如何互动是一个非常复杂的对话，

sentences.en: how to carry himself, how to speak, when to speak, what to do with his hands.
sentences.zh: 如何举止、如何说话、何时说话、手该放在哪里。

sentences.en: All of these sort of prescriptive things that we talk to him about so that he knows what to do and that he can make smart decisions when being confronted by police officers.
sentences.zh: 所有这些我们告诉他的指导性事项，都是为了让他知道该怎么做，以便在面对警察时能做出明智的决定。

sentences.en: And he worries that his life expectancy is short.
sentences.zh: 他担心自己的寿命很短。

sentences.en: And he said that to me when he was eight.
sentences.zh: 他在八岁时就对我这么说过。

sentences.en: And he's talked about it recently.
sentences.zh: 最近他也谈到过这一点。

sentences.en: And he said, you know, am I going to live to 30?
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，我能活到30岁吗？

sentences.en: And what did you say back?
sentences.zh: 那你怎么回答他的？

sentences.en: What did I say back?
sentences.zh: 我怎么回答的？

sentences.en: I said, that's a reality that is hard.
sentences.zh: 我说，这是一个残酷的现实。

sentences.en: And as a mother, it's hard to have this conversation.
sentences.zh: 作为母亲，进行这样的对话很艰难。

sentences.en: But yes, you can live to your more than 30.
sentences.zh: 但是的，你可以活到30岁以上。

sentences.en: But that the reality is no matter what he does, some people will still look at him as a threat to society.
sentences.zh: 但现实是，无论他做什么，有些人仍然会把他视为对社会的威胁。

sentences.en: He remembers when he was cute.
sentences.zh: 他还记得自己小时候很可爱的样子。

sentences.en: He was still cute at seven.
sentences.zh: 他七岁时还是很可爱。

sentences.en: But once he became eight or nine, people started grabbing their purses on elevators when we got on elevators.
sentences.zh: 但当他长到八九岁时，当我们走进电梯，人们就开始抓紧他们的钱包。

sentences.en: Just two weeks ago in our own neighborhood when we were walking our dog, he was behind me and some of our neighbors followed him because he had a mask on.
sentences.zh: 就在两周前，在我们自己的社区遛狗时，他走在我身后，一些邻居因为他戴着口罩就跟踪他。

sentences.en: And he said, well, mom, how do I protect myself from disease when people are looking at me as a criminal?
sentences.zh: 他说，妈妈，当人们把我当成罪犯时，我该如何保护自己免受疾病侵害？

sentences.en: And I said, carefully, gingerly, and do the best you can at being who you are, being proud of who you are,
sentences.zh: 我说，要小心、谨慎，尽你所能做你自己，为你自己感到骄傲，

sentences.en: but also being careful that not everybody see you as the beautiful child that I gave birth to and that my husband and I have raised.
sentences.zh: 但也要小心，并不是每个人都把你视为我所生、我和我丈夫所抚养的那个美丽的孩子。

sentences.en: So in this cycle of joy and pain that has always been Juneteenth, which way does it lean for you and for your family this year?
sentences.zh: 那么，在六月节这一贯穿始终的喜悦与痛苦的循环中，今年对你和你的家人来说，它更倾向于哪一边？

sentences.en: Joy or pain?
sentences.zh: 喜悦还是痛苦？

sentences.en: Pain.
sentences.zh: 痛苦。

sentences.en: Absolutely pain.
sentences.zh: 绝对是痛苦。

sentences.en: We're hurt by the ways in which African-Americans are being hurt in this country.
sentences.zh: 我们为这个国家非裔美国人所受到的伤害而感到心痛。

sentences.en: We're hurt that all of the battles of freedom and for equality, we're hurt that no matter what we do, we're still being treated with the level of disrespect
sentences.zh: 我们为所有争取自由和平等的斗争感到心痛，我们心痛的是，无论我们做什么，我们仍然受到那种不尊重的对待，

sentences.en: that harkens back to earlier periods in American history.
sentences.zh: 这种对待让人回想起美国历史上的早期时期。

sentences.en: I teach an African-American history class called Intro to African-American History, and it covers African arrival in what became the United States until today.
sentences.zh: 我教授一门名为《非裔美国人历史导论》的课程，内容涵盖从非洲人抵达后来成为美国的地方直到今天。

sentences.en: It's a big sweeping time period.
sentences.zh: 这是一个跨度很大的时期。

sentences.en: But students often are exhausted by the time we reach the 20th century because of the highs and lows that African-Americans have experienced in this country.
sentences.zh: 但学生们往往在学到20世纪时就感到精疲力竭，因为非裔美国人在这个国家经历了太多的起伏。

sentences.en: I remember one student asking me, where is the Black joy?
sentences.zh: 我记得有个学生问我，黑人的喜悦在哪里？

sentences.en: When do we get to see Black joy?
sentences.zh: 我们什么时候才能看到黑人的喜悦？

sentences.en: And I said, we're coming up to the Harlem Renaissance.
sentences.zh: 我说，我们马上就要讲到哈莱姆文艺复兴时期了。

sentences.en: There's lots of joy in that decade.
sentences.zh: 那个十年里有很多喜悦。

sentences.en: But then it follows by the Great Depression and the Jim Crow legislation and lynching.
sentences.zh: 但随后紧接着就是大萧条、吉姆·克劳法案和私刑。

sentences.en: And so once we have a high, then it ebbs down into a low valley of despair and pain.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦我们经历了一个高峰，它就会回落到绝望和痛苦的低谷。

sentences.en: And students are saying again, Dr. Berry, we're getting exhausted.
sentences.zh: 学生们又说，贝里博士，我们感到精疲力竭。

sentences.en: We're going back into this period of despair.
sentences.zh: 我们又回到了这个绝望的时期。

sentences.en: And then there's a resurgence of the civil rights movement and the Black Power movement.
sentences.zh: 然后民权运动和黑人权力运动又出现了复兴。

sentences.en: And we have another sort of swing upward.
sentences.zh: 我们又经历了一次上升。

sentences.en: But as a historian, I wonder, in this moment, it's hard to interpret historical moments when we're in them.
sentences.zh: 但作为一名历史学家，我感到好奇，在当下，当我们身处其中时，很难解读历史时刻。

sentences.en: But I wonder what we'll say about today, 50 years from now.
sentences.zh: 但我好奇50年后我们会如何评价今天。

sentences.en: Will we say that there was a change or is this another high or another low that we've experienced and we go back to business as usual?
sentences.zh: 我们会说发生了改变，还是说这只是我们经历的又一个高峰或低谷，然后一切又照旧？

sentences.en: I like to think, because I'm an optimist, that there will be change and that we will come out of this low moment as a better people and a better society.
sentences.zh: 我倾向于认为，因为我是个乐观主义者，会有所改变，我们将作为一个更好的民族和一个更好的社会走出这个低谷。

sentences.en: When you think about Juneteenth as the day that finally brought freedom to enslaved people in Texas,
sentences.zh: 当你把六月节视为最终为德克萨斯州的奴隶带来自由的日子时，

sentences.en: how do you think about freedom in this moment?
sentences.zh: 你如何看待当下的自由？

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: For me, when I think about Juneteenth as Emancipation Day, and I think about this moment,
sentences.zh: 对我来说，当我把六月节视为解放日，并思考这个时刻时，

sentences.en: I feel like we still need to be emancipated.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们仍然需要被解放。

sentences.en: There's still more freedoms that need to be protected.
sentences.zh: 还有更多的自由需要被保护。

sentences.en: There's still more laws that need to be revised.
sentences.zh: 还有更多的法律需要被修订。

sentences.en: There's still more inclusion that needs to happen.
sentences.zh: 还有更多的包容需要实现。

sentences.en: There's still more achievement to be had.
sentences.zh: 还有更多的成就需要达成。

sentences.en: There's still more space for change and growth.
sentences.zh: 还有更多的空间需要改变和成长。

sentences.en: And so for me, on today, on Juneteenth,
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，在今天，在六月节，

sentences.en: I'm reflecting on how can I, in my little corner of the world, make change happen and make generations that come after me experience some more just and whole society.
sentences.zh: 我正在反思我如何在自己小小的世界角落里推动变革，让下一代体验到一个更加公正和完整的社会。

sentences.en: And I spend the day reflecting on that and having conversations with my husband and my son and trying to encourage him to have hope and faith in the future.
sentences.zh: 我花了一整天时间反思这一点，并与我的丈夫和儿子交谈，试图鼓励他对未来抱有希望和信念。

sentences.en: Dr. Berry, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 贝里博士，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me on this historic day.
sentences.zh: 感谢你在这样一个历史性的日子邀请我。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: The Times reports that global daily infection rates from the coronavirus reached record highs over the past week,
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》报道称，过去一周全球新冠病毒日感染率创下历史新高，

sentences.en: driven by outbreaks in Latin America, Africa, South Asia, and the United States.
sentences.zh: 主要受拉丁美洲、非洲、南亚和美国的疫情驱动。

sentences.en: In Brazil, officials reported more than 32,000 new cases on Wednesday, the most in the world.
sentences.zh: 在巴西，官员周三报告了超过32000例新病例，为全球最高。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: reported the second most, more than 25,000.
sentences.zh: 报告了第二高，超过25000例。

sentences.en: Within the U.S., California and Florida reported their highest daily infections yet on Thursday, prompting California to require the state's 40 million residents
sentences.zh: 在美国国内，加利福尼亚州和佛罗里达州周四报告了迄今为止最高的单日感染人数，促使加州要求该州4000万居民

sentences.en: to cover their faces in almost all settings outside the home.
sentences.zh: 在家庭以外的几乎所有场合都要遮住面部。

sentences.en: And...
sentences.zh: 还有……

sentences.en: I have sent a letter to the clerk of the House, directing the clerk to remove the portraits of four previous speakers of the House who served in the Confederacy.
sentences.zh: 我已经致信众议院书记官，指示书记官撤下四位曾在邦联服役的前众议院议长的肖像。

sentences.en: In Washington, House Speaker Nancy Pelosi announced that she would take down the portraits of four previous House speakers who had served in the Confederacy.
sentences.zh: 在华盛顿，众议院议长南希·佩洛西宣布，她将撤下四位曾在邦联服役的前众议院议长的肖像。

sentences.en: One of them, James Orr of South Carolina, had vowed on the floor of the House to, quote, preserve and perpetuate slavery.
sentences.zh: 其中一位，来自南卡罗来纳州的詹姆斯·奥尔，曾在众议院议事厅发誓要，引用其原话，“维护并延续奴隶制”。

sentences.en: There's no room in the hallowed halls of this democracy, this temple of democracy, to memorialize people who embody violent bigotry and grotesque racism of the Confederacy.
sentences.zh: 在这个民主的神圣殿堂，这个民主的圣殿里，没有空间去纪念那些体现了邦联暴力偏执和荒谬种族主义的人。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《地铁》节目中，我，莎拉·凯尼格，将为您讲述那些试图维持影响力却在过程中逐渐失控的人们的故事。
